root_cause.finding: The integrated controller started the 160-second readiness deadline at controller entry, before the independently startup-budgeted CUDA peer probe, worker imports, and retained-engine model-load start. The phase budget defines readiness from retained-engine startup, so startup work was incorrectly deducted from the engine readiness window.
contributing_evidence: Both worker processes remained alive until the controller issued SIGTERM; their observed return codes were -15, not spontaneous engine failure codes.
Both vLLM logs show the pinned Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct model loaded and both engines reached initial profiling/warmup before the timeout.
Neither log contains a Python exception, CUDA fault, vLLM engine-core failure, or worker-initiated exit.

The v4 diagnostic log path was slower than v3 before strict readiness: model-resolution logging moved from approximately 18 seconds after worker logging began to approximately 33 seconds, while torch.compile moved from 40.90/41.01 seconds to 47.90/48.52 seconds. These wall-clock log deltas are diagnostic only; the authoritative failure is the controller timeout evidence.

serving_work_audit.conclusion: Attempt v4 contains topology, engine-initialization logs, failure, settlement, and cleanup diagnostics only. It provides no new 12-rps, 15-rps, control, recovery, queue-drain, restore-interference, or transaction metric.

local_fix.description: Each retained worker now emits an immutable startup barrier immediately before real model construction. The controller validates both PID/UUID-bound barriers, derives the readiness deadline from the earliest real model-load timestamp to match the historical phase definition, retains the absolute controller cap, and emits the clock evidence in controller-result.json.

budget_audit.reasoning: The v4 client-visible startup/import evidence invalidates reuse of the old 135-second startup upper bound and yields a 1,176-A100-second adjusted rerun estimate. The current live ledger cannot satisfy current_conservative_usage + required_A100_seconds <= configured_hard_ceiling even under the superseded 938-second estimate. The controller fix does not authorize weakening the evidence-derived reservation or increasing the configured ceiling.

open_findings.finding: No scientifically valid v10 transaction exists, and the ledger has insufficient remaining authorization for the evidence-derived rerun reservation.
Because the controller source changed, any future attempt must commit the fix and regenerate the code-commit-bound immutable authorization and dependent pre-GPU reviews before launch.
The 135-second startup upper bound is stale against v4's client-visible startup/import proxy; any future phase budget must incorporate the post-v4 evidence and be independently reviewed.
